findings.finding: F1 (owner-only): dispatch://INFRA-747's carry note section 4, carried to dispatch://INFRA-757, keeps envoy-go-race as the docs-only job and moves the other packages out, which collides with this issue's design over job names.
findings.answer: The plan follows INFRA-756's acceptance, which pins the other arrangement (docs in 'a job of its own'; 'the new job has its own filter (the docs package's closure)'); it names the job envoy-go-race-docs and the filter envoy_go_race_docs, which fit INFRA-757's own envoy-go-race-<group> table, so its rebase keeps its four jobs and drops the line that renames envoy-go-race. The plan's Coordination section records this and the planner reports it to the architect, which owns telling INFRA-757's tree.

findings.finding: F2: the acceptance never names Postgres, and a docs race job without DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL would be green having skipped nearly every test (storetest.Open calls t.Skip, storetest.go:57-61; persistence_test.go:19 makes storetest.Main the package TestMain).
findings.answer: T2 copies the services.postgres block and the env from ci.yaml:2280-2292 and says it is load-bearing; acceptance 3a's check reads the job log for `ok  github.com/sjawhar/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs  <N>s` and for the absence of the 'DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL must be set' line; negative control 3 shows that skip locally.

findings.finding: F3 (owner-only part): the race lane is red on main today on internal/bus (TestADrainEndsTheKVWatchersBeforeTheConnection, drain_kv_watcher_test.go:27, in run 40877712458 at 14d907b6 - the very job the spec's Evidence cites), so acceptance 3's 'the remaining race lane passes' is not in this change's control.
findings.answer: The plan's rule for 3b: a required red returns the issue to implementing, the implementer traces it by test name, re-runs the failed jobs once (the one re-run pr-body.md allows), records the run ids and the trace under Not proven / risk, and reports it to the architect naming dispatch://INFRA-750 as the owner. No role fixes a bus race here. Recorded as this plan's one spec departure, for the architect to settle.

findings.finding: F4: the 1773 s baseline was measured with other race binaries on the same runner (job 123461966609: six package times summing to 5125 s inside 1842 s of step wall), and 'its measured time' names no number; docs has 625 top-level tests and two t.Parallel() calls, so it will not use the freed cores itself.
findings.answer: The plan defines the measured time as the package line `ok  .../internal/dispatch/docs  <N>s` plus the job's wall time, both quoted with run and job ids, and gives the off-CI re-run command. It states that -timeout 60m and timeout-minutes 70 stand whatever the number is, since acceptance 1 fixes them, and records the contention reading as the reason the number may fall far below 1773 s.

findings.finding: F5 (owner-only): the spec's Evidence is wrong in two ways - the cited baseline job failed on internal/bus, not on time, and the 69 lines at job 123503246603 are failures (62 from the test binary's deadline), not tests refused by a time guard; acceptance 4's third non-goal has no subject, since both docs time guards already t.Fatalf.
findings.answer: The plan records all three as corrections in its own 'Corrections to the spec's Evidence' section and the planner names them in the completion summary; the spec stays as approved and nothing the plan builds changes.

findings.finding: F6: hidden requirements a router job carries - no Bun, the cache question, the timeout arithmetic in a comment, the old job's stale prose and pinned step name, draft/merge-queue/concurrency/required-check behaviour, and a second Postgres service.
findings.answer: T2 states each: no Bun (no subprocess in the package), a restore-only go-envoy cache in dispatch-browser-multiprocess's shape (ci.yaml:1980-1990), timeout-minutes 70 with its arithmetic in a comment, an if: with no github.event_name term and no concurrency of its own, and no ruleset change since only ci-ok is required. T3 rewrites the old job's comment, step name and the stale 880 s figure, and T6 adds the ci.yaml cache-family sentence. The second Postgres runs on its own runner and storetest clones a template database per test.

findings.finding: F7: check-ci-filters.sh never fails a filter that is wider than the closure, so copying envoy_go_race's packages/envoy/** would pass; the narrow closure is the plan's choice and rests on hand-kept RULES.
findings.answer: The plan chooses the narrow closure, because a wide filter would run a 20-to-30-minute race job on every packages/envoy change, which is the parent issue's whole point, and records the grep that verified the docs package's out-of-package reads (only ci_job_reads.py:258-260 are unconditional; the corpus-gated reads stay out, as the router page says).

findings.finding: F8: removing one package from envoy-go-race forces an edit of the gate's pinned step name, text and package list, and no filter edit; neither check-ci-filters.test.sh nor ci-ok.test.sh reads the real table, so no test must be extended.
findings.answer: T5 moves the step name and the pinned text with the step, T3 keeps the envoy_go_race filter except the decision-blocks pattern (whose only reader in packages/envoy is docs/approval_carry_test.go:26), and T7.2 still runs both script tests as a cheap sanity check.

findings.finding: F9: four prose places state what the lane is - packages/envoy/AGENTS.md:661-664 and :2454, ci.yaml's go-envoy cache sentence, and docs/testing.md:40-42, which names a workflow file this repository no longer has.
findings.answer: T6 edits all four, the docs/testing.md path correction included, and notes that INFRA-757 also rewrites the two AGENTS.md lines, so the edits stay minimal and contiguous.

findings.finding: F10: acceptance lines no machine could check as written - the total test set, 'the closure as the drift check computes it', the measured time and the remaining lane.
findings.answer: The plan's acceptance table gives each a command: a go list diff for the total set (T7.4), the drift check's '24 gates, 0 uncovered' plus a PathsFilter selection proof with three positive and three negative paths (T7.1, T7.5), the job log's package line for the time, and the 3b rule above for the remaining lane.
